title: Counting and Radix Sort
summary: Sorting without comparisons - counting sort for small key ranges and how prefix sums make it stable, radix sort digit by digit (least significant digit first) for integers and fixed-length strings, bucket sort for evenly spread values, when these linear-time sorts beat std::sort, and a summary of every sort in the milestone.

cards.q: Why does LSD radix sort need a stable sort for each digit?
cards.a:
To keep the order earlier passes made

Keys that tie on the current digit must stay in the order the previous, less significant passes produced.

cards.q: Counting sort on n = 1,000 values whose keys range up to k = 1,000,000,000 is...
cards.a:
A poor choice: O(n + k)

O(n + k) is dominated by the billion counters. Counting sort only pays off when k is not much bigger than n; radix sort splits such keys into small digits instead.
